# engine

## Releasing the engine

- **Planning a release** — several sessions work here at once and each release costs a full gate
  run, so before you start the work that will need one, add a line to
  `/mnt/project-files/release-flow/release-intents.md`: your thread, the PRs it will ship, and
  what it still waits on. Read the other lines while there, and keep yours current as the work
  moves. (planning-release)

- **Another thread also plans one** — whichever finishes last releases both changes, then clears
  both lines once its release run is green. The thread that finishes first marks its line "done,
  waiting for <thread>" and does not dispatch. (another-thread-plans)

- **No one else plans one** — the first thread to reach its release point releases. A thread
  whose change lands after that release runs its own. (no-one-else-plans)

- **Tempted to release because someone else is** — don't: a thread releases only when its own
  change needs shipping. Never dispatch a release, or merge early, because another thread's
  release is near. (never-release-because)

- **Waiting on another thread's release** — only while its line shows it still working and not
  blocked. Once it finishes, goes stale (no change in its line or its PRs for a day) or is
  blocked on a person, release your own change and say so on its line. (never-wait-forever)

## The update flow

- **Discussing, designing or reviewing a change to how members receive engine or pack
  updates** - answer from `docs/update-flow.md`, its requirements, limits and open questions,
  rather than re-deriving the flow from code; a proposal that breaks one of its `UF-n`
  requirements names the id and goes to Ariel before it is code. (update-flow-doc-first)

## Standing owner decisions

- **Designing or describing what Claudinite is** — its unit of adoption is the *repository*: it
  pins a `cn`, declares packs in `.claudinite/settings.yaml`, runs its own tasks and validates
  its own state. A per-user or per-machine framing (a plugin, a developer's install) is a
  category error that invents costs the real shape lacks. (designing-describing-claudinite)

- **Having a deferred direction, blocked proposal or status to record** — put it under `docs/`
  and point at it from the issue or PR; never in a pack's `RULES.md`, `SKILL.md`, `README.md` or
  manifest, which ship to every member. (having-deferred-direction)

- **Ending a session on unfinished work** — never compose a hand-off prompt; the owner's opener
  is `continue work on #<n>`. (ending-session-unfinished)

- **Designing anything that spans repos** — split it: a per-repo half that reads and judges one
  repository knowing nothing of any other, and an aggregation half under `cn/fleet` that
  enumerates the owner's repositories at run time. No repository list lives in code.
  (designing-anything-spans)

- **Needing a member to flip a platform setting** — last resort; per-repo manual work reliably
  does not happen. Prefer a route that works with the job's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`, or neutralise
  the blocking behaviour's effect, before asking for a reconfiguration. (needing-member-flip)

- **Releasing a change members must receive** — force delivery (a `fleet/fleet-update` item from
  the manager) only where *"will it work on every repo?"* is live: the update itself, the
  settings contract, a workflow template, a new settings key. Otherwise the scheduled engine
  update is the delivery. (landing-change-members)

- **Retiring a field, option or verb** — mark its definition `// Deprecated:` and comment each
  sanctioned holdout with why it still carries it. Keep the contract validating it; never write
  a bespoke conformance check for a deprecation. (retiring-field-option)

- **Designing a standing mechanism that detects a problem and could act on it** — ship the
  detection alone: a finding names its probable causes, says when that set is open, and
  recommends; the fix stays a gated step, since a mitigation chosen from an inferred cause
  reapplies itself every cycle. (designing-standing-mechanism)

- **Surfacing a number a human reads as a report card** — report a window against the previous
  window; never a monotonic cumulative total, never a figure nothing measures.
  (surfacing-number-human)

- **Lacking a field a report-card number needs** — name it absent in the surface's own note. A
  stated gap is information, a guess is not. (lacking-field-report)

- **Windowing a count** — only where it is built from things that happened inside the window. A
  figure derived from a point-in-time stamp reads a steady population as declining.
  (windowing-count)

- **Classifying an open object by deriving it from other live state** — reconsider once the
  derivation's inputs can change while the object stays open, silently rewriting its history.
  Prefer a marker stamped once at creation and never revisited. (classifying-open-object)

## Working with the owner and the session's tools

- **Answering "why did it fail?"** — lead with the throwing call site: `file:line`, the
  function, and which side enforced it. A narrative that never names the line reads as
  unanswered. (answering-did-fail)

- **Wanting to re-post a question the owner declined** — don't. Take its recommended default, or
  open the question up. (wanting-re-post)

- **Asking about a vague, destructive-sounding instruction** ("remove the entire mechanism") —
  scope the question to the boundary of the vague noun itself, not the consequences of one
  reading of it. (asking-vague-destructive)

- **Writing an `AskUserQuestion`** — phrase it and its options in the requirement's own plain
  terms, not internal jargon, and give an axis the owner treats as independent its own option
  rather than folding it into another. (writing-askuserquestion)

- **Writing the reason an `AskUserQuestion` option gives for itself** — verify it against the
  call sites first: the owner picks the option *for* that reason, so one that proves false is
  this change's to make true, not a new decision to take back. (writing-reason-askuserquestion)

- **Putting a design, restructure or plan to the owner for approval** — render the end state
  whole, every element kind it touches rather than the one easiest to show, and name the
  decisions it took that they never asked about. (putting-design-restructure)

- **Being asked to generalise something, or to review it** — land the conversions or action
  points it unlocks in the same change: a capability ships with its first caller, an analysis
  with its first recommendation applied. (being-asked-generalise)

- **Calling any `claude-code-remote` tool** — one call per intent, ever. Each costs minutes, and
  a call that returns nothing has not failed. (calling-anything-claudecoderemote)

- **Needing to read issues or PRs across several repos in one session** — `add_repo` widens this
  session's GitHub scope; issues are not git refs, so a clone is no substitute.
  (needing-session-read)

- **Reading a tool result the harness saved to a file** — an MCP result is one unbroken line, so
  `Read`'s `offset`/`limit` won't shrink it; parse it with `jq` or `python3 -c
  'json.load(...)'`. A saved Bash result is ordinary lines. (reading-tool-result)

- **Re-waiting on a signal that already failed to move** — read the code that governs when it
  *can* change before waiting a second time on the same premise. (re-waiting-signal)

- **Replying to an owner comment that raises more than one claim** — answer every claim in that
  first reply, including the one you intend to push back on. (answering-every-claim)

- **Repeating a design doc's stated architectural rationale** — verify each claimed ground
  against the current code first; a later `docs/design-record.md` row may have amended it.
  (repeating-design-docs)

- **An owner reversing a standing decision** — purge every place that still states the old
  decision (docs, comments, code defaults) and record the new one where a future session reads
  it (in the engine, a `docs/design-record.md` row that amends the old). Answering the prompting
  question alone is not the fix. (owner-reversing-standing)

- **A Bash command refused as naming git (or a computed argument) "too complex to verify" inside
  a worktree-isolated agent** — drop straight to the plain, literal form; a loop, heredoc or
  `$(...)` around the same call fails the same way. (bash-command-refused)

- **Bundling a file write into a Bash command that also runs a guarded call** (`go test`, `git
  commit`, `curl`) — split them: a PreToolUse guard reads the whole command string, heredoc data
  included, and blocks the call before any of it runs, so the write is lost.
  (bundling-write-guarded)

- **Calling `EnterWorktree` in an unattended session** — nobody is present to approve it, so it
  is denied after about a minute; use `git worktree add` or `git checkout -b` instead.
  (calling-enterworktree-unattended)

- **Finishing a fan-out of subagents** — clear its wreckage before reporting done: stop the
  waiters, confirm each child's commits are on your branch, and remove its worktree and branch.
  (finishing-fan-out)

- **Asserting why a system behaved a certain way** — read the primary evidence first: the
  issue's own body and comments, or the enforcing source line. A verdict inferred from structure
  or memory alone has shipped as a fix for a bug that wasn't there. (asserting-system-behaved)

## Checks and capabilities

- **Starting a new Claudinite capability** — decide its home before the first file: `cn` code, a
  pack the engine carries (`cn/*/pack`), a canon pack in ClaudinitePacks, or a member's local
  pack. Getting it wrong costs a move-and-rewrite across repos. (starting-new-claudinite)

- **Naming a function** — a `<verb><noun>` name reads as doing that verb to that noun, so give a
  reader a verb that says it reads (`readWindowCommits`) and never lead with a noun that is also
  a verb (`commitFiles`). (naming-function)

- **Naming a key in the declared-check vocabulary** (`specKeys` in
  `cn/checks/declared/vocab.go`) - name it so a declaration reads alone (`scanFiles`,
  `matchLines`, `relevantWhen`); if it needs a comment to be read, it needs a better name.
  (declaring-check-adding)

- **Adding a property to a declared vocabulary** (the task contract in
  `cn/capabilities/tasks/taskspec`, the check vocabulary) — judge it on its own terms: a
  validation, default or behaviour that reads a SIBLING property's value needs the owner's
  explicit permission first, and so does prose describing it that way. The existing pairs
  (`automerge`/`expected_outcome`, `agent_instructions`/`agent_model`,
  `code_work_timeout`/`code_work`) stand. (adding-property-declared)

- **Choosing how a declared field spells two opposite states** — never let them differ by one
  keystroke (`["none"]` vs. no key); a reader without the schema must still tell them apart.
  (choosing-declared-field)

- **Adding a legacy tolerance for a rename whose holders are files this session can read** —
  count them and rename them in the same change instead; a dual read is scaffolding where the
  old spelling may have one holder. (legacy-tolerance-holder-count)

- **Adding a legacy tolerance in code** — file the issue that removes it first, then put
  `@legacy-tolerance advisory:<rule-id|none> retire:#<issue>` in a comment directly above the
  declaration; `advisory:none` claims no member file can hold the old shape, so that issue must
  name what does read the holder. (legacy-tolerance-marker)

- **Creating the artifact a check will demand** — create it before the action it gates, not
  after. (creating-artifact-check)

- **Writing the exemption branch of a check** — read its evidence from the tracked tree, never
  the change's own files: the change an exemption spares is usually one that never touches the
  file carrying the evidence. (writing-exemption-branch)

- **Writing a check that fires on a removed line** (`forbidRemovedLinesMatching`) — it cannot
  see a deleted file: removing one export fires, deleting the whole file is silent. Guard the
  deletion separately. (writing-check-fires)

- **Wanting a boundary enforced in test files** — never a `forbidReferences` barrier, whose
  scanner drops every `*.test.mjs` first; express it as a line-match check, which does see
  tests. (wanting-boundary-enforced)

- **Changing a per-call hook path** (`cn/integrations/hooks`, a guard, a forced-loading hold) —
  measure it before and after with the hook-latency probe (`dev/test/packs.sh` runs it with
  `--budget`) and keep it inside the budgets the package states. (changing-call-hook)

## The engine and what reaches members

- **Editing the scheduler or executor workflow templates**
  (`cn/capabilities/tasks/workflows/templates/`) — nothing beyond triggers, permissions,
  concurrency and one-line `run:` steps calling `.claudinite/bin/cn <verb>`. A workflow change
  reaches members only through a reviewed workflow PR, so logic belongs in `cn`.
  (editing-claudinite-scheduler)

- **Tightening a contract member-owned files must satisfy** (`settings.yaml`, a local pack's
  manifest, a `task.json`) — no update rewrites member files beyond the settings edits
  `cn/packaging/updateedits` carries, so accept the old shape at load, permanently, and
  normalize it at the door. (tightening-contract-member)

- **Adding a key to the declared-check vocabulary** — an older `cn` drops the key and runs the
  rest of the declaration, so write the declaration correct without it, or raise the pack's
  `minEngineVersion` to the first `cn` that reads it. (adding-key-declared)

- **A stale member declaration** — fail the run; never let it degrade to fewer checks running.
  (stale-member-declaration)

- **Renaming a pack's config key that members write into `settings.yaml`** — every reader
  resolves the new key and every legacy spelling, permanently; nothing rewrites a member's
  settings for a pack. (renaming-pack-config)

- **Renaming or removing anything in the check SDK or `@claudinite/sdk` that a pack calls** —
  keep the old name working: packs on the shelf and in members run against older and newer
  engines, gated only by `minEngineVersion`. (renaming-deleting-engine)

- **Asking which SDK symbols packs still use** — read ClaudinitePacks' `main` and the pack
  versions members hold, never `--all` refs: a call that only existed on an unmerged branch is
  not fielded. (asking-imported-symbols)

- **Excluding files from the vendored archive by pattern** — whitelist any operational file that
  matches by path, and pin it with a test against the real shelf; a published pack version is
  immutable, so a file it dropped stays missing for every member holding it.
  (excluding-files-vendor)

- **Testing that an operational file still vendors** — assert the whole containing directory,
  not the one file that broke. (testing-operational-file)

- **Retiring or reshaping a protocol cn exposes** (a verb a workflow calls, a worker RPC, a
  `wake` input, a settings key) — sweep for callers outside this repo (members' workflows,
  ClaudinitePacks), not just what greps here. (retiring-reshaping-protocol)

- **Branching on the result of a GitHub API write** — read its status, not just the body; a
  body-only decode turns a 403 into a plausible object and the run still logs ok.
  (branching-result-api)

- **Judging whether a migration chain's link is still outstanding** — read the world its exit
  condition names, never the link's own issue, whose status lags the world.
  (judging-whether-migration)

- **A single timeout bound covering two different waits** ("has this started" vs "is something
  running about to finish") — split it, sizing each from that phase's own declared budget.
  (single-timeout-bound)

- **Writing a give-up message for a hit timeout** — say it is a statement about the clock, not a
  verdict on the work. (writing-give-up)

- **Writing generated content into a size-capped GitHub field** — budget it in two tiers: an
  always-complete compact summary, plus detail rationed to a byte budget with an explicit
  omitted-count; an unbounded write fails at ~64KB. (writing-generated-content)

- **Writing a generated title whose content scales with a list** — collapse the list to a count
  and keep per-item detail in the body. (writing-generated-title)

- **Preflighting a required grant or permission** — a probe run where the failure's condition
  isn't met reports a false pass; prefer attributing a real observed 403 to the permission that
  would fix it. (preflighting-required-grant)

- **Introducing a finer-grained classification of a catch-all state** — default whatever an
  older or unaware writer produces to the most conservative member of the new set.
  (introducing-finer-grained)

- **Adding a fleet task or verb** — fail loudly on a target it cannot reach rather than
  proceeding on a partial list, and treat a repo as outside the fleet until `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`
  reaches it; a drift that completes files a report reading as a full sweep. (adding-fleet-task)

- **Spawning a child process** (a worker, git, the checks binary) — set its working directory
  explicitly from the repo root the command was given, never the inherited process cwd.
  (spawning-child-process)

- **A worker crash sharing a benign outcome code** — keep "could not run" distinguishable from
  "had nothing to run", or the crash is unobservable. (worker-crash-sharing)

- **Reading a uniform signal across every fleet member** — check for a rate-limit signal before
  trusting a uniform empty sweep, and check whether each member's own update window has passed
  before calling the fleet frozen. (reading-uniform-signal)

- **Corroborating a theory with a signal already known unreliable** — don't; find an independent
  one. (corroborating-theory-signal)

- **Retiring or moving a dispatch or Context parameter** — a parameter that stops being read
  must fail loudly, never silently default; a dropped safety knob (`DRY_RUN`) defaults to the
  operation's most dangerous mode. (retiring-migrating-dispatch)

- **Renaming a cn verb or launcher path a member workflow names** — keep the old one working
  until every member's workflows moved: `.github/workflows/` changes only through a reviewed PR.
  (workflow-file-referencing)

- **A script written for one execution context** — audit every script's environment assumptions
  (a real `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `gh`/`curl` reachability) whenever its caller's context changes; every
  script built on the old assumption fails the same way. (script-written-execution)

- **Carrying a version** (`1.61004.1`) — keep it string-typed everywhere and compare it part by
  part; `'60820.10'` and `'60820.1'` are different versions and the same float.
  (carrying-dotted-version)

- **Changing the format of an identifier members compare for order** — choose the new shape so
  every old value sorts below every new one, and the change needs no migration and no tolerance.
  (changing-format-identifier)

- **Designing text that instructs a model to echo an exact string** — state the instruction
  first, have it disclaim itself as instruction-not-payload, and put the literal string once,
  last; never refer to it anaphorically. (designing-text-instructs)

## Scheduled tasks

- **Changing how the scheduler asks tasks** (`cn/capabilities/tasks/schedule`, a precondition
  term) — re-audit every task on the shelf and in the engine-carried packs whose preconditions
  assumed the old behaviour, by its precondition text, not only the changed code's callers.
  (scheduler-mechanism-flip)

- **Writing a backstop, fallback lane or sweep whose healthy run finds nothing** — give it a
  term that asks its own question, calling the rules its worker calls rather than restating
  their clocks; a cadence alone files an item and a closed receipt every period to say all is
  well. (writing-backstop-fallback)

- **Passing a diagnostic verdict out of a subprocess that may be killed at its timeout** — write
  it to stdout or stderr as you go, never a file written at exit; printed output survives a
  kill. (passing-diagnostic-verdict)

- **Building a dedup or mutex over work items** — key it on the target the write lands on, never
  the requester's phrasing; a same-title match is blind to two items writing one target under
  different titles. (building-dedup-mutex)

- **Re-delivering a scheduled recompute onto its own branch** — compare the branch's remote tree
  with the one you built and push nothing when they match; a force-push gives the PR a new head
  and discards every check already run on it. (re-delivering-scheduled)

## Proving a change

- **Needing a pack, task, skill or check name in a test** — use the invented `acme-pack`,
  `acme-task`, `acme-skill`; a pack's own tests name its own elements freely, and a line whose
  subject really is a real entity ends `@real-entity <why>` in a comment.
  (test-fixtures-use-fake-entities)

- **Testing a change to a task's triggering** — drive the real `schedule.Plan` from a clock at
  which the task's anchor has NOT come; starting from a queued item proves only "works once
  filed". (testing-change-tasks)

- **Testing a fail-soft step** — assert the positive effect (the output IS emitted), never a
  clean exit, which fail-soft makes meaningless. (testing-fail-soft)

- **Testing a mechanism that arbitrates by identity** (a claim, a lock) — the second call must
  come from a *different actor*. (testing-mechanism-arbitrates)

- **Building a simulator for a stateful engine mechanism** (`cn/capabilities/tasks/sim`) — model
  what the code actually writes, never the rule's stated intent. (building-simulator-stateful)

- **Asserting a mid-run invariant** — capture it at the moment the state holds; by the run's end
  normal convergence has cleared the evidence. (asserting-mid-run)

- **Writing a conformance test over the tree or the shelf** — gather every failure and report
  once (`t.Errorf`, not `t.Fatal`, inside the loop), so one change touching five places costs
  one red-green cycle. (writing-conformance-test)

- **Writing a regression test that pins a policy or convention** — assert the behaviour the
  decision requires, never a sentence quoted from a doc. (writing-regression-test)

- **Deriving an answer by walking git history** — guard explicitly against a shallow clone and
  fail loudly; otherwise it answers from the clone's own horizon. (test-derives-answer)

- **Changing the guidance that produced a bad artifact** — prove the rewrite by reverting that
  artifact and having a fresh subagent redo the task against the new text.
  (changing-guidance-produced)

- **Restoring source after a deliberate see-it-fail mutation** — stage your own edits to that
  file first, then `git checkout -- <file>` at the moment of mutating, never a backup taken
  earlier. (restoring-source-deliberate)

- **Surveying whether something exists in the tree** — a code-search hit is evidence, a miss is
  not; survey by reading each file. (surveying-whether-something)

- **Documenting or relying on a named knob** — grep for the code that reads it and the code that
  writes it first; the corpus naming it is not evidence it exists. (documenting-relying-named)

- **Deleting a writer** — mark its series historical in the same change; its rows otherwise keep
  counting plausibly until retention ages them out. (deleting-writer)

- **Renaming an entity** — don't change historical records. (renaming-entity)

- **Sweeping a rename across several PRs** — a file added after the sweep starts can reintroduce
  the retired name as a comparison key, failing silently; re-grep at the end.
  (sweeping-rename-mid)

- **Renaming a word that is also stored data** (a counter key, a wire word, a label) — rename it
  on the decode side too, or old rows decode to null. (renaming-word-also)

- **A second rename of one name** — map every legacy spelling straight to today's, never
  chaining one normalization onto the last. (second-rename-name)

- **Writing a "this period is covered" marker** — write it strictly after the durable effect it
  guards, and only for the declined case; a go verdict's coverage is the item it created.
  (writing-period-covered)

- **Verifying a bulk file-move or rewrite preserved content** — compare a structural count
  before and after (`func Test` or `test(` calls across the touched files); a truncated test
  file still passes. (verifying-bulk-file)

## Editing, branching and merging

- **Opening a pull request** — open it as a draft and mark it ready for review once the work is
  done: CI and claudinite-ci skip drafts, so every push before that costs no run.
  (opening-pull-request)

- **Rewriting a JSON or YAML target nested inside an array within an entry** — parse and rewrite
  structurally, preserving key order and sibling fields; an anchored regex cannot cross the
  nested closing bracket. (json-target-nested)

- **Returning to a branch that waited** — after `git fetch`, re-verify the premise unasked: say
  whether the problem is still there and what survives. (returning-branch-waited)

- **Merging a PR that sat open across many `main` commits** — check its current
  `mergeable_state`, not an old green run; a move on `main` can make it conflict with no new run
  failing. (merging-pr-has)

- **A PR head showing no check runs at all** — read its mergeability first: GitHub starts no
  `pull_request` run while the branch conflicts with its base. (pr-head-no-checks)

- **Scoping a fix to the lines a change added when it also moved files** — drop the pathspec:
  narrowed to the destination, `-M` has no source to pair and reports every moved line as added.
  (scoping-fix-added-lines)

- **Rebasing a branch that moved files onto a `main` that edited them** — git raises the
  conflict at the old path only, so resolving it for the move drops `main`'s hunks; audit them
  before pushing. (rebasing-branch-moved)

- **Having work that completes or corrects an open PR** — put it on that PR's branch; splitting
  gives the owner two gates for one decision. (having-work-completes)

- **Wanting to combine two PRs** — update the one you keep and close the other; never push one's
  branch onto the other's base, since GitHub marks a PR merged once its head is reachable.
  (wanting-combine-prs)

- **Being asked "should no X decide this?"** — it questions whether the decision exists at all;
  never answer by moving the knob one rung out. (being-asked-should)

- **Facing a retry across a call whose outcome you cannot observe** — check whether declining to
  retry removes the uncertainty before building dedup machinery. (facing-retry-across)

- **Writing a regex import-path rewriter for a bulk move** — anchor to real import syntax, never
  a bare `from '...'` across the whole text; fixtures holding import syntax as data get
  corrupted. In Go, prefer `gofmt -r` or `go` tooling. (writing-regex-import)

- **Verifying a sweep that rewrote citations** — read every rewritten site, not just the exit
  grep, which proves the old token gone, never the replacement right. (verifying-sweep-rewrote)
</system-reminder>

{"number":168,"title":"cloudflare-site: a build's watch_dir counts toward a release","body":"The `site-release` gate (`unreleased-commits`) counts a commit only when it touches a deployed path: the wrangler config, the published tree, the Worker's folder or the package manifests. That misses everything for a site whose published tree is build output. In missingbulb/NoRFinder, `build.command` runs `dev/tools/build/build.py`, which fills `dev/build/site/` from `web/` and `studies/`, and git ignores that tree. So none of its page changes counted. A forced release (missingbulb/NoRFinder#602) declined with "changed nothing the deploy ships", and the site only released after a placeholder commit (missingbulb/NoRFinder#603).

### Change
- With a non-empty `build.command`, `deployedPaths` adds the config's `build.watch_dir`, resolved from the config's folder. That is Wrangler's own field for what a build reads ([docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/#custom-builds); the resolution is from `normalizeAndValidateBuild` in workers-sdk). An entry may be a file or a folder, so a path without a trailing `/` now matches as either.
- If the build names no usable `watch_dir` (missing, empty, not a string, or covering the whole repo or reaching outside it), `deployedPaths` returns `null`, and the gate already counts every commit then. Wrangler's own `./src` default is deliberately not used, since a build that reads from elsewhere would never release.
- The first version of this PR counted every commit in a repo with a build, which undid the narrowing there. That approach is listed as rejected in the provenance entry.
- The task README says which commits count, and that a site whose build reads from outside the published tree sets `watch_dir`.
- The pack version goes to `1.61031.1`, which `release-plan` requires, and the directory row is re-rendered.

### `provenance/_pack.md`: the version entry was appended by hand
`_pack.md` ends on the 2026-10-05 `retired` entry for `migrations/`, and `cn provenance append` refuses any entry after a `retired`. The blocking `provenance-change-recorded` check required an entry, and only accepts a file that grows at its end. So the base text stays as it was and the bump's entry follows it, written by hand in the tool's own format. Both `cn check work-and-world` and `cn provenance check cloudflare-site` pass. Claudinite/Engine#556 makes both provenance checks advisory, and makes the tool warn rather than refuse in a case like this. `github-pages` and `public-website` also end their `_pack.md` on that retirement.

### Tests
- `lib.test.mjs`: `watch_dir` as a string, a list and a parent-relative path, a file entry, each unusable `watch_dir`, and `watch_dir` with no or blank command.
- `preconditions.test.mjs`: a commit under `watch_dir` releases, a near-miss (`tools/build.pyc` against `tools/build.py`) and a docs commit don't, and with no `watch_dir` every commit releases.
- The new tests failed before the change. Each refusal guard was weakened in turn and a test went red. All 321 Node tests run: 319 pass and 2 skip. `release.mjs plan --content` and `cloudflare-site`'s Go checks pass. `tools/checks/test.sh` as a whole fails at vet in `executable-requirements`, which this PR doesn't touch: the local engine's SDK lacks `Turn.Branches`.
- On NoRFinder's last 60 commits, with `watch_dir: ["web", "studies", "dev/tools/build"]`, every product change counts. Engine bumps, Claudinite housekeeping, product-wiki pages and session-history commits don't.

### Follow-up in NoRFinder

{"number":168,"title":"cloudflare-site: a build's watch_dir counts toward a release","body":"The `site-release` gate (`unreleased-commits`) counts a commit only when it touches a deployed path: the wrangler config, the published tree, the Worker's folder or the package manifests. That misses everything for a site whose published tree is build output. In missingbulb/NoRFinder, `build.command` runs `dev/tools/build/build.py`, which fills `dev/build/site/` from `web/` and `studies/`, and git ignores that tree. So none of its page changes counted. A forced release (missingbulb/NoRFinder#602) declined with "changed nothing the deploy ships", and the site only released after a placeholder commit (missingbulb/NoRFinder#603).

### Change
- With a non-empty `build.command`, `deployedPaths` adds the config's `build.watch_dir`, resolved from the config's folder. That is Wrangler's own field for what a build reads ([docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/#custom-builds); the resolution is from `normalizeAndValidateBuild` in workers-sdk). An entry may be a file or a folder, so a path without a trailing `/` now matches as either.
- If the build names no usable `watch_dir` (missing, empty, not a string, or covering the whole repo or reaching outside it), `deployedPaths` returns `null`, and the gate already counts every commit then. Wrangler's own `./src` default is deliberately not used, since a build that reads from elsewhere would never release.
- The first version of this PR counted every commit in a repo with a build, which undid the narrowing there. That approach is listed as rejected in the provenance entry.
- The task README says which commits count, and that a site whose build reads from outside the published tree sets `watch_dir`.
- The pack version goes to `1.61031.1`, which `release-plan` requires, and the directory row is re-rendered.

### `provenance/_pack.md`: the version entry was appended by hand
`_pack.md` ends on the 2026-10-05 `retired` entry for `migrations/`, and `cn provenance append` refuses any entry after a `retired`. The blocking `provenance-change-recorded` check required an entry, and only accepts a file that grows at its end. So the base text stays as it was and the bump's entry follows it, written by hand in the tool's own format. Both `cn check work-and-world` and `cn provenance check cloudflare-site` pass. Claudinite/Engine#556 makes both provenance checks advisory, and makes the tool warn rather than refuse in a case like this. `github-pages` and `public-website` also end their `_pack.md` on that retirement.

### Tests
- `lib.test.mjs`: `watch_dir` as a string, a list and a parent-relative path, a file entry, each unusable `watch_dir`, and `watch_dir` with no or blank command.
- `preconditions.test.mjs`: a commit under `watch_dir` releases, a near-miss (`tools/build.pyc` against `tools/build.py`) and a docs commit don't, and with no `watch_dir` every commit releases.
- The new tests failed before the change. Each refusal guard was weakened in turn and a test went red. All 321 Node tests run: 319 pass and 2 skip. `release.mjs plan --content` and `cloudflare-site`'s Go checks pass. `tools/checks/test.sh` as a whole fails at vet in `executable-requirements`, which this PR doesn't touch: the local engine's SDK lacks `Turn.Branches`.
- On NoRFinder's last 60 commits, with `watch_dir: ["web", "studies", "dev/tools/build"]`, every product change counts. Engine bumps, Claudinite housekeeping, product-wiki pages and session-history commits don't.

### Follow-up in NoRFinder
missingbulb/NoRFinder#613 sets `build.watch_dir`. Until it lands, NoRFinder releases on every commit: that's correct, just not narrowed.

content.text:
{"number":613,"title":"wrangler.json: name the build's inputs as watch_dir","body":"The nightly site release counts a commit only when it touches a path the deploy ships. Here the published tree, `dev/build/site/`, is build output that git ignores, so no page change ever counted. That's why the forced release in #602 declined, and why #603 and #607 were placeholder commits.

This sets `build.watch_dir` to `["web", "studies", "dev/tools/build"]`, the folders `build.py` reads from. Claudinite/PublicPacks#168 teaches the gate to count commits under `watch_dir`.

### Before and after Claudinite/PublicPacks#168 reaches the mount
- **Now:** the mounted gate ignores `watch_dir`, so releases behave as before. This PR touches `wrangler.json`, which is a shipped path, so it releases the page changes that have built up since 0.11031.62.
- **Once #168 is in the mount:** a commit under `web/`, `studies/` or `dev/tools/build/` releases. One that touches only `docs/`, `product-wiki/` or `.claudinite/` doesn't. On the last 60 commits of `main`, this counts every product change, and engine bumps, housekeeping and wiki pages don't count.

### Checks
- `wrangler@4.128.0 deploy --dry-run` (the release's pinned version) accepts the config and runs the build.
- `web-tests/test_published_site.py` passes, 13 of 13.

### Side effect on `wrangler dev`
`watch_dir` also tells `wrangler dev` what to watch, and `build.py` writes into `web/` (`vendor/`, `studies.json`, `version_history.json`). So a `wrangler dev` session would probably rebuild in a loop. Nothing here runs `wrangler dev`, since local preview is `http.server`, so this only matters if someone starts using it.

content.text:
{"number":556,"title":"Provenance is a record to keep, not a format to enforce: its checks advise and the tool warns","body":"Provenance files keep the history of how a pack changed, so that later reviews can confirm or overturn each decision. What matters is that the entries exist, neither too few nor too many. The format isn't the point. Two format rules were getting in the way of that record. In Claudinite/PublicPacks#168:
- the blocking `provenance-change-recorded` demanded a `_pack.md` entry for a version bump;
- `cn provenance append` refused to write one, because the file's last entry was a `retired`, which sealed it;
- so the entry could only go in by hand.

### What changes
| Mechanism | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provenance-change-recorded` | block | advise |
| `provenance-integrity` | block | advise |
| `append`/`apply`: unknown kind or field, bad date, missing title or Mechanism, out of date order, after a `retired`, first entry not `born`, text that is not exactly one entry | refused | written, each fault printed as `<file>: warning: …` |
| `append`: an entry that reads as a secret | refused | refused |
| `append`: a path under the vendored mount | refused | refused |
| `append`: an element no carrier names | refused | refused: the entry would land where nobody reads it, which loses the record |
| `--backfill` lane | refuses a malformed batch | unchanged: it re-renders the whole file, so it can't take text it can't parse |
| one change keeps one entry per element (the fold) | folds | unchanged: it keeps entries from piling up |

These skills now say "advises" and "warns" instead of "blocks" and "refuses": `changing-pack-elements`, `backfilling-provenance` and `writing-pack-prose`. Each of those elements, and both checks, gets an entry. The decision is row 221 of `docs/design-record.md`.

### Left alone, for you to decide
- `cn provenance check` still exits 1 on a fault. It's a report command, and nothing in CI gates on it, so I didn't change it.
- `Backfilled` still refuses a `retired` entry that isn't its file's last, and two `born` entries in one file. Only the backfill lane uses it.

### Tests
- **Checks:** every `want` in both checks' tests now expects advisory. They failed (25 findings still blocking), then passed after the `OnFail` change. `TestBuiltinsListAndRunUnderTheirPack` lists the two checks as `advise`.
- **Tool:** `TestAppendWritesAFirstEntryThatIsNotBornAndWarns`, `TestAppendWritesAnEntryTheGrammarFaultsAndWarns` (six faults) and `TestApplyWritesAnEntryAfterARetirementAndWarns` failed before the change. The `apply` test fails again with the old refusal put back. `TestAppendOfAGoodEntryWarnsOfNothing` pins the silent case. The secret, unknown-element and vendored-mount tests are unchanged and pass.
- **Suites:** `dev/test/test.sh -short -count=1 -p 8` passes, 138 packages. `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean on `cn/provenance`. I couldn't run golangci-lint or shellcheck here because neither is installed; this diff touches no shell. I didn't run the full suite.

### Release
I couldn't add a line to `release-intents.md`, because this session can't reach `/mnt/project-files`. Members get the change with the next engine release.

---

input.title: Release on page commits: watch_dir in wrangler.json, and the gate from PublicPacks#168 in the mount
input.body:
The nightly site release counts a commit only when it touches a path the deploy ships. Here the published tree, `dev/build/site/`, is build output that git ignores, so no page change ever counted. That's why the forced release in #602 declined, and why #603 and #607 were placeholder commits.

### Change
- `wrangler.json` sets `build.watch_dir` to `["web", "studies", "dev/tools/build"]`, the folders `build.py` reads from.
- The mounted `cloudflare-site` pack carries the gate from Claudinite/PublicPacks#168, which counts a commit under `watch_dir`. Three files are copied as they are in #168: `lib.mjs`, `tasks/site-release/preconditions.mjs` and that task's README. Before the copy, they matched the published 1.61020.2 exactly. This is a hand-edit of `.claudinite/shared/`, which the owner asked for so releases work without waiting for a full pack update. `shared-tree-immutable` and `claudinite-files-changed` will advise against it.

### What happens next
- **Merging this** releases the page changes that have built up since 0.11031.62, because `wrangler.json` is a shipped path.
- **From then on**, a commit under `web/`, `studies/` or `dev/tools/build/` releases. One that touches only `docs/`, `product-wiki/` or `.claudinite/` doesn't.
- **The next "Claudinite update"** replaces the mount whole. Once #168 is published (cloudflare-site 1.61031.1), that update brings the same code. If an update lands before #168 is published, it puts the old gate back.

### Checks
- The patched gate, run in this checkout: it reads `wrangler.json, dev/build/site/, package.json, package-lock.json, web, studies, dev/tools/build`. On the last 40 commits of `main`, 31 count, up from 15 with the published gate. Every page change counts. Claudinite updates and housekeeping, the session-history commits and the product-wiki page don't.
- `wrangler@4.128.0 deploy --dry-run` (the release's pinned version) accepts the config and runs the build.
- `web-tests/test_published_site.py` passes, 13 of 13. The gate's own tests ran in #168 against these same files.

### Side effect on `wrangler dev`
`watch_dir` also tells `wrangler dev` what to watch, and `build.py` writes into `web/` (`vendor/`, `studies.json`, `version_history.json`). So a `wrangler dev` session would probably rebuild in a loop. Nothing here runs `wrangler dev`, since local preview is `http.server`, so this only matters if someone starts using it.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/PublicPacks/.claude/skills/merge-to-main

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Capture the conversation: `.claudinite/bin/cn growth capture --pr <pr>`. Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
6. Run the task-flow pack's
   `verify-in-production` skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

The merge leaves the local checkout on the branch it squashed, and no step here syncs `main`; the
merge is usually a session's last act. Only if you go on to start further work in this session,
sync first, before branching off anything:

```
git fetch origin main && git checkout main && git reset --hard origin/main && git remote prune origin
```
